text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Peter Kiss, chairman of the Socialist Party's financial supervising committee, said no unchecked funds had been transferred to Socialist coffers, and the party does not plan an investigation in connection with the Tocsik scandal. @

- After the session of the Free Democrats' national council President Ivan Peto observed that while the Tocsik scandal undoubtedly affects Free Democrats figures, and does harm to the party, as a party the Free Democrats are not involved in the issue.

- All parliamentary parties except the Socialists believe that settlement of the controversial issue of the Gabcikovo hydroelectric power plant is only feasible via the upcoming trial at the International Court of Justice.
- Parliament is set to reconvene for its spring session on February 3. @
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn pledged on Friday to find a solution for settling the HUF 3.4 billion in debts accumulated by the Hungarian police force. (Sat.)
- The Ministry of Industry together with the Ministry of Finance is analysing the possibility of setting up a bank for small and medium-sized enterprises.
- With capital of $930 million, MOL ranks 11th on the Financial Times' list of the 50 largest companies in Central and Eastern Europe.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin said his country would prefer Szeged as the site for reopening the Romanian consulate. (Sat.)
- The government is planning to integrate the contribution-collecting branches of the tax authority APEH with those of the social insurance funds (pension and health care).

- Hungary brought in foreign exchange revenues of more than $2 billion between January and November last year, 31 percent more than in the same period of 1995, a preliminary report by the National Bank of Hungary reveals. @

- The New York Times claimed Friday that a new divide - a "second iron curtain" - has been created in Central and Eastern Europe, putting on one side the more economically advantaged and socially balanced countries closer to Western Europe, on the other side there are the poorer countries.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Ministry of Defence will finalise this week the technical details for utilisation of a $5 loan million granted by the US government for the regional airspace management system. @
- This paper reports that Hungary will apply for a corporate and financial restructuring loan worth $225 million to the board of directors of the World Bank in early March.
- Transport Minister Karoly Lotz Friday named Bela Szalai as ministerial commissioner to handle tension which have arisen following dissatisfaction over toll rates on the M5 motorway.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Employees of companies in Hungary spend 49 percent of their time at work unproductively - or an annual 110 working days - a study by the efficiency consultancy company Czipin & Partner reveals. @
NAPI GAZDASAG
- A total of 11 million tons of grain was produced in Hungary last year, some 1 percent more than in 1995.
- The nuclear power plant Paksi Atomeromu closed last year with pre-tax profits of HUF 250 million on turnover of HUF 46.7 billion. (Sat.)
